name: Wiscon Industries
summary: Wiscon Industries is a Delhi-based company, incorporated in September 2022, that trades and distributes LED TVs, air coolers, washing machines and ACs under its own Wiscon brand and sells third-party electric scooters; it recently acquired LED TV maker Dalmia Technologies as a wholly owned subsidiary. Consolidated revenue jumped from ₹3.2 cr in FY24 and ₹14.5 cr in FY25 to ₹196.9 cr in FY26, with profit of ₹20.4 cr in FY26, but most of that jump comes from the acquired subsidiary and operating cash flow was negative ₹20 cr in FY26. Of the ₹88 cr fresh issue, only ₹15 cr (17%) funds new machinery while ₹52 cr goes to working capital; promoter Sidhant Dalmia also sells ₹22 cr through the offer for sale. At the upper band the post-issue P/E on FY26 profit is about 20x, roughly 26% above the only listed peer named in the RHP, Cellecor Gadgets.

fh1.finding: Consolidated revenue rose from ₹3.21 cr (FY24) to ₹196.87 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 683%, largely from the acquired subsidiary.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹3.21 cr, ₹14.49 cr, ₹196.87 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.96 at June 2026 (borrowings ₹36.97 cr vs net worth ₹38.49 cr), up from 0.83 in FY26.

fh4.finding: Borrowings and revenue on the same (consolidated) basis across FY24–FY26 were not found in public sources.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: about −₹0.34 cr (FY24), ₹4.17 cr (FY25), ₹30.61 cr (FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was negative at −₹20.01 cr in FY26, against a profit of ₹20.41 cr.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax rose from ₹1.25 cr in FY25 to ₹20.41 cr in FY26, helped by the subsidiary acquisition.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from a loss in FY24 to about 8.6% (FY25) and 10.36% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 66.67% in FY26, on a small equity base.

pr5.finding: FY26 net margin of 10.36% vs about 3.1% for the only listed peer, Cellecor Gadgets (₹39.61 cr profit on ₹1,292 cr revenue).

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 20.0x on FY26 profit (₹407.75 cr market cap / ₹20.41 cr) vs 15.89x for the only peer, Cellecor Gadgets, about 26% above.

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 3.2x (₹407.75 cr market cap vs about ₹126.5 cr post-issue net worth) vs 3.89x for Cellecor Gadgets.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: No details of pre-IPO share issues or transfers and their prices were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 68.46% after the issue, down from 94.18%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters was found.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹22 cr, or 20% of the ₹110 cr issue.

is2.finding: The issue is about 27% of the ₹407.75 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: Promoter Sidhant Dalmia sells in the OFS, but his average acquisition cost was not found in public sources.

up1.finding: Only ₹15.04 cr (17.1%) of the fresh issue funds new plant and machinery at the subsidiary; ₹52 cr goes to working capital.

up2.finding: None of the fresh issue is earmarked for repaying debt.

up3.finding: General corporate purposes take ₹15.74 cr, or 17.9% of the fresh issue.

up4.finding: No proceeds go to repaying loans, from promoters or anyone else.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: Top 10 customers made up 63.36% of recent revenue.

rk2.finding: Top 10 suppliers made up 99.77% of recent purchases, called out as a risk; single-supplier shares are not published.

rk3.finding: Incorporated in September 2022, so about 4 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
